concepts.def: y = aˣ with a > 0, a ≠ 1. Grows rapidly if a > 1; decays if 0 < a < 1. Always passes through (0, 1).
y = eˣ where e ≈ 2.71828. Unique property: d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ. Used for continuous growth/decay.
logₐ x is the inverse of aˣ: logₐ x = y ⟺ aʸ = x. Natural log: ln x = logₑ x.
log(xy) = log x + log y; log(x/y) = log x − log y; log(xⁿ) = n log x. Same base throughout.
logₐ x = logᵦ x / logᵦ a. Useful when calculator only has log₁₀ or ln.
Population growth, radioactive decay, Newton's law of cooling: all use y = Aeᵏᵗ. Log transforms linearise data.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Exponentials & Logarithms — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Exponentials & Logarithms brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Exponentials & Logarithms.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between congruent and similar shapes?
options: Congruent and similar both mean 'the same shape' — they're interchangeable.
Congruent shapes are identical in size and shape; similar shapes have the same shape but can be different sizes (scaled).
Congruent shapes are similar with different angles.
The x value where the line crosses the x-axis.

mcqs.q: In the equation y = 3x + 5, what does the 5 represent on the graph?
options: The y-intercept — the value of y when x = 0 (where the line crosses the y-axis).
The x value where the line crosses the x-axis.
The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
The gradient — how steep the line is.
